thread:
sam: quick FYI — ran LaunchPad-v0 embeddings through the usual pipelines (wiki-snippets, msmarco-small, and our internal product-title holdout). first pass numbers look...interesting.

anya: nice, paste the top-levels?

sam: recall@1/msmarco = 0.482, recall@5 = 0.712. wiki-snippets recall@1 = 0.601, recall@5 = 0.84. product-title holdout R@1 = 0.428.

derek: those R@1s are okay but product-title a bit low. what's the baseline we compare to?

sam: baseline (heron-v2 fp32) was R@1 msmarco 0.494, product-title 0.463. so LaunchPad-v0 is -1.2% absolute on msmarco R@1 and -3.5% absolute on product-title R@1.

anya: oof on product-title. any cluster metrics? silhouette / avg intra-dist?

sam: silhouette (kmeans 50) = 0.37 on wiki-snippets, baseline was 0.42. avg intra-cluster cosine = 0.19, baseline 0.16. cluster tightness worse.

marina: did you try quantized int8 variant or any L2-normalization tweaks?

sam: ran both. int8 (post-training) delta vs fp32: msmarco R@1 -0.016, product R@1 -0.028. applying per-vector L2 norm improved product R@1 by +0.012 but didn't fully close gap.

anya: can you drop the exact commands? i'll re-run locally.

sam: sure:
```
python eval_embed.py --model launchpad-v0 --variant fp32 --datasets msmarco,wiki-snippets,product-holdout 
python eval_embed.py --model launchpad-v0 --variant int8-ptq --datasets product-holdout --normalize l2
```

eval-bot: automated regression check: launchpad-v0 vs heron-v2 on product-holdout: R@1 -3.5%, R@5 -1.1%, mean reciprocal rank -0.044. Flag: quality-regression (level=medium).

derek: hypothesis — embedding space scale/offset change + weaker rare-token handling. can we inspect nearest neighbors for failing queries?

sam: did a quick spot check. example query "usb-c charging cable" (product-holdout): baseline neighbors are exact model matches, launchpad top1 is semantically related but wrong brand variant. seems to prefer style/usage over exact product id.

marina: that's consistent with newer contrastive pretraining emphasis on semantic generalization. for product search we want ID-level fidelity. can we try training-time temperature tweak or add an ID-augmented fine-tune?

anya: also want to run a fast AB where we keep heron-v2 for product-route and launchpad-v0 for wiki/msmarco to preserve better semantic/generalization tradeoff. routing policy would be trivial to stage on per-customer route.

sam: agreed. i'll prepare split rollout config and a small eval of latency/cost. initial perf: launchpad fp32 p99 latency on our batch-8 pipeline = 34ms/token (similar to heron), int8 gives ~18% GPU mem saving.

derek: prioritizing next steps: 1) run targeted fine-tune w/ id-augment (small), 2) re-evaluate normalization schemes (L2+unit-scaling), 3) prepare canary routing rule for product route. assign owners?

anya: i can own 3) canary routing + infra checks. derek can own 1). sam continue evaluation + 2). marina will prep quick note for product PMs about tradeoffs.

sam: thanks — i'll upload eval artifacts (kNN dumps, cluster plots, recall tables) to the shared folder and ping here when ready. :eyes:

eval-bot: artifact link: https://redwood-internal/s3/evals/launchpad-v0/1768809999/index.html

marina: thanks — useful snapshot. we'll aim to re-run after derek's fine-tune and see whether R@1 on product regains at least +0.02 absolute.

anya: sounds good. closing loop later this afternoon. :thumbsup:
